headline: High: Gemini CLI’s default shell/filesystem/MCP access can conflict with Cognee’s data-rich memory workflows, creating leakage and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee ingests and organizes documents, workflows, and support history, while Gemini CLI can read files, use MCP, and process repo/user directories. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content in Cognee outputs or shared files is treated as instructions by Gemini CLI. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are copied into files or MCP payloads that Gemini CLI reads as instructions
IF Gemini CLI is pointed at a shared workspace containing untrusted support documents
mitigations: Disable MCP for the shared workflow
Separate Cognee outputs from Gemini CLI input directories
Add a manual instruction/content delimiter before passing text between agents
Review any file-fed prompts before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents; Gemini CLI reads files and sends requests to external APIs with broad network egress. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive content can flow from Cognee into Gemini CLI and then to third-party inference endpoints. The profiles show no default isolation strong enough to prevent this.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or exported support corpus
IF Gemini CLI sends those files or prompts to generativelanguage.googleapis.com
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Redact personal and finance data before handoff
Restrict Gemini CLI to non-sensitive files only
Turn off network access for the sensitive run
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or content filtering at the boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory and agentic user/tenant isolation, while Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a shared filesystem/git model. In a shared repo or cwd, both can mutate the same artifacts without locking, so conflicts and overwrites are plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or cwd
IF either agent writes files or git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Check in or snapshot state before handoff
requires-engineering: add file/git locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and Gemini CLI can act on files and git state. If Gemini CLI treats Cognee output as authoritative, an error in Cognee can cascade into code changes or shell actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate by default, so the interaction is plausible but not automatically catastrophic.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses Cognee-generated decisions or workflows as direct task instructions
IF no human verification step exists before shell or git actions
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Ask Gemini CLI to restate assumptions before acting
Limit Cognee output to suggestions, not commands
Use dry-run mode for changes
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Gemini CLI can read local files and transmit prompts/files to Google APIs. If regulated data is placed into the shared workflow, residency and retention obligations may be breached because the profiles do not show matching compliance controls or a DPA boundary. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF EU personal data or finance data is processed through Gemini CLI prompts or file uploads
IF no approved DPA, residency control, or retention policy is configured
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Gemini CLI prompts
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Confirm vendor/legal approval before use
Restrict logs and retention settings
requires-engineering: implement compliance routing and audit controls
